subject: general
question: Hool Diwas is celebrated on June 30 every year in India to commemorate the Santhal Hool (rebellion) of _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1855**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Santhal Hool (rebellion) took place in **1855** and was one of the most significant tribal uprisings against the British colonial rule in India.
 
• The rebellion was led by the **Santhal brothers – Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, and Bhairav Murmu**, who mobilized the Santhal community.
 
• The Santhals rose in revolt due to exploitation by **zamindars, moneylenders, and the British revenue policies**, which caused severe hardships to the tribal community.
 
• On June 30, 1855, the Santhal leaders formally declared rebellion against the British and their allies by organizing a meeting at **Bhognadih** in the present-day state of Jharkhand.
 
• The rebellion was eventually suppressed by the British using military force, but it became a symbol of tribal resistance and is commemorated annually as **Hool Diwas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key examples of other significant tribal revolts:**

 
 
• **Munda Rebellion (Ulgulan) (1899-1900):** Led by the iconic Birsa Munda in the Chotanagpur region, it aimed to establish Munda Raj and fight against land alienation and forced labor.
 
• **Kol Rebellion** (1831): Occurred in the Chota Nagpur region, protesting land acquisition and the influx of non-tribal people.
 
• **Bhil Uprisings **(Various times, e.g., 1825-1857): A series of revolts by the Bhil people in Western India against British encroachment and new revenue systems.
 
• **Chuar Uprising **(1768-1816): Known as the Jungle Mahal Revolt in Bengal, it involved farmers and hunters resisting high revenue demands and alien rule.
 
• **Rampa Rebellion** (1922-1924): A major revolt in the Rampa region of Andhra Pradesh led by Alluri Sitarama Raju against forest laws and forced labor.
 
• **Paika Rebellion** (1817): An armed uprising in Odisha against the British land revenue policies.
